questions.stem: During negotiation, the seller tells the listing broker to remove a printed paragraph from a Commission-approved form. How should the broker show the deletion?
choices: Erase or white out the paragraph so the final form looks clean
Retype the form without the paragraph in the same font
Strike through the text so it can still be read
Leave the text in place and explain the change to the parties in an email
questions.explanation: Printed text is deleted only because of negotiation or a party's instruction, and it is struck through so it remains legible. It is never silently erased or retyped away.

questions.stem: A broker inserts an attorney-drafted clause into the Additional Provisions of a contract. Under Commission rules, how long must the broker keep a copy of that clause, with the attorney's name?
choices: 4 years from its last use
1 year from closing
3 years from its first use
For as long as the broker holds a license
questions.explanation: Commission rules require the broker to keep an attorney-drafted clause, with the attorney's name, for 4 years from its last use and to provide it to the Commission on request.

questions.stem: The buyer's lender approves the loan, but the interest rate offered is higher than the buyer is willing to accept. Under the Colorado residential contract, which deadline should the buyer use to terminate?
choices: New Loan Availability Deadline
Appraisal Objection Deadline
New Loan Terms Deadline
New Loan Application Deadline
questions.explanation: Unsatisfactory loan terms such as the rate are handled by the New Loan Terms Deadline, in the buyer's sole discretion. The New Loan Availability Deadline is for an unsatisfactory underwriting result and can't be used for problems with the loan terms.

questions.stem: A buyer makes an offer. The seller responds with a Counterproposal, which the buyer lets expire. The seller now wants to sign the buyer's original offer. What is the result?
choices: The original offer revives automatically once the counterproposal expires
The seller can't accept it, because the counterproposal rejected the original offer
The seller can accept it by signing before the original Acceptance Deadline
The seller can accept it by sending an Agreement to Amend/Extend
questions.explanation: Under general contract law, a counteroffer rejects the original offer, so that offer is gone. The parties would need a new offer or counterproposal.

questions.stem: A contract terminated when the parties failed to sign an Inspection Resolution by the Inspection Resolution Deadline. Two days later, both parties want the deal back on. Which Commission form fits?
choices: Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract
Inspection Objection Notice
Earnest Money Release
Agreement to Revive Contract
questions.explanation: A terminated contract can't be amended, because nothing is left to amend. The Agreement to Revive Contract brings it back: the parties state the termination date, ratify the contract and set new deadlines.

questions.stem: A seller already under contract receives a better offer and wants to accept it. How should the second contract be structured to avoid two binding contracts?
choices: As a backup offer that depends on the first contract terminating
As a counterproposal that supersedes the first contract
As an Agreement to Amend/Extend the first contract with the new buyer's terms
As a new contract signed first, with a Notice to Terminate sent to the first buyer afterward
questions.explanation: A seller who accepts a second offer should make it a backup offer contingent on the first contract terminating. Otherwise the seller risks being bound to two contracts.

questions.stem: A buyer's broker has submitted an offer, but the listing broker won't respond to calls or emails. What should the buyer's broker do first?
choices: Deliver the offer directly to the seller
File a complaint with the Real Estate Commission
Contact the listing broker's employing broker
Have the buyer withdraw the offer and resubmit it later
questions.explanation: The buyer's broker goes to the listing broker's employing broker first. Only if that fails does the buyer's broker go to the seller directly.

questions.stem: A seller signs the Exclusive Right-to-Sell Listing Contract but checks neither the seller agency box nor the transaction-brokerage box. What is the broker's relationship with the seller?
choices: Seller's agent
Transaction-broker
Dual agent for the seller and any buyer
No brokerage relationship until a box is checked
questions.explanation: If neither relationship box is checked in the listing contract, the broker is a transaction-broker.

questions.stem: An HOA board wants to fine an owner for leaving trash cans out. The association has no written fine policy. Under CCIOA, what is the board's position?
choices: It may fine the owner if the rules and regulations prohibit the conduct
It may fine the owner after a majority vote of the owners
It may fine the owner only up to six months of regular assessments
It can't fine the owner without a written policy providing notice and a hearing
questions.explanation: An HOA can't fine an owner without a written fine policy that gives notice and an opportunity to be heard. Associations must adopt written governance policies, including a covenant-enforcement policy.

questions.stem: An owner is fully paid up on assessments but owes the HOA $3,000 in fines, late charges and interest. Can the association foreclose its CCIOA lien based on that balance?
choices: Yes, once the balance equals six months of assessments
No, those items alone can't be the basis of a CCIOA foreclosure
Yes, if the board records a vote authorizing the foreclosure
No, because fines can't be secured by the HOA lien at all
questions.explanation: Fines, fees, late charges and interest can be secured by the lien, but they can't by themselves be the basis of a CCIOA foreclosure. Foreclosure requires a lien balance of at least six months of common-expense assessments plus a recorded board vote.

questions.stem: In general, the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act applies to common interest communities created:
choices: on or after July 1, 1992
before January 1, 1970
only after its 2015 amendments
on or after January 1, 2000
questions.explanation: CCIOA applies to communities created on or after July 1, 1992, with limited exceptions. Older communities are reached only by the specific sections listed in C.R.S. 38-33.3-117.

questions.stem: A buyer pays all cash for a Colorado home, so there is no lender and no federal Closing Disclosure. What closing document must the broker still make sure the buyer receives?
choices: A loan estimate prepared by the title company
An accurate closing statement signed by the broker
No closing document, because a cash sale has no federal disclosure
A Closing Disclosure prepared by the listing broker
questions.explanation: A cash sale has no Closing Disclosure, but every transaction, cash or financed, still needs a closing statement. The broker must see that the consumer receives an accurate, complete closing statement signed by the broker.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Real Property Transfer Declaration (TD-1000) filed with a Colorado deed?
choices: It calculates the documentary fee owed to the state
It notifies the county treasurer that taxes have been paid
It informs the assessor of the sale price
It gives public notice of the buyer's ownership
questions.explanation: The TD-1000 is filed with the deed so the assessor learns the sale price. The clerk sends it to the assessor, and it is not a public record.

questions.stem: A buyer wants protection against unrecorded mechanics' liens and matters a survey would show. What should the buyer ask for under the Colorado contract?
choices: Owner's extended coverage
A lender's title policy
A certificate of taxes due
A standard owner's policy
questions.explanation: Owner's extended coverage (OEC) removes the standard exceptions, such as unrecorded mechanics' liens and survey matters. The contract states whether OEC is provided and who pays the extra premium.

questions.stem: Which person can manage rental property for compensation in Colorado WITHOUT a real estate broker's license?
choices: An independent manager who leases homes for several owners for a percentage of rents
A regularly salaried on-site manager of an apartment building doing customary duties
A person who lists a neighbor's condo for rent online for a flat fee
An employee of an investor who leases the investor's scattered single-family homes for a fee
questions.explanation: The exception is narrow: a regularly salaried employee of the owner of an apartment building or condominium units who acts as the on-site manager, doing only customary on-site duties. Leasing for others for compensation otherwise requires a license, even as the owner's employee.

questions.stem: A property management firm collects a tenant's rent on Monday. Within what time must the firm deposit it into its rent trust account?
choices: One business day
Three business days
Ten calendar days
Five business days
questions.explanation: Property management funds must be deposited within five business days after receipt (or after the lease is signed, if later). The three-business-day deadline applies to other trust money such as earnest money.

questions.stem: A landlord keeps part of a tenant's security deposit for carpet damage but never sends a written statement listing the reasons. What is the consequence under Colorado law?
choices: The landlord forfeits the right to keep any part of the deposit
The landlord may keep the amount if the damage is documented with photos
The landlord must pay a $500 penalty but may keep the deduction
The tenant must sue within 7 days or the deduction stands
questions.explanation: A landlord who fails to deliver the written statement of reasons within the deadline forfeits the right to keep any part of the deposit. The 7-day figure is the notice a tenant gives before suing for willful retention, not a deadline to sue.

questions.stem: A tenant gives proper written notice of a condition that materially interferes with life, health or safety. Under Colorado's warranty of habitability, when must the landlord begin fixing it?
choices: Within 96 hours
Within 24 hours
Within 10 days
Within 30 days
questions.explanation: For a condition that materially interferes with life, health or safety, the landlord must respond within 24 hours and begin remedial action within 24 hours. The 96-hour window is for other conditions that make the unit uninhabitable.

questions.stem: A tenant is two months behind on rent. The landlord changes the locks while the tenant is at work, without a court order. What is the landlord's position under Colorado law?
choices: The lockout is lawful because the rent is more than 30 days late
The lockout is lawful if a 10-day demand was served first
It's unlawful, and the tenant can recover damages and attorney fees
It's unlawful only if the lease bans lockouts
questions.explanation: Removing or locking out a tenant without court process is unlawful. The tenant can recover actual damages plus the greater of three months' rent or $5,000, and attorney fees, no matter how much rent is owed.

questions.stem: A covered residential tenant has lived in a Colorado apartment for two years and has followed the lease. The landlord simply prefers a new tenant and wants to decline to renew. Under Colorado's for-cause eviction law, what is the general rule?
choices: The landlord may decline with 10 days' written notice
The landlord may decline at the end of any lease term
The landlord generally needs cause or a qualifying no-fault reason
The landlord may decline only if rent rises above market
questions.explanation: Colorado's 2024 for-cause law generally requires a landlord to have cause, or a qualifying no-fault reason with longer written notice, to refuse to renew a covered tenant who has lived in the unit 12 months or more. The details have since been amended, but the principle holds: simply preferring a new tenant isn't a reason.

questions.stem: A buyer is acquiring shares in a mutual ditch company along with a farm. How do those shares transfer?
choices: By a recorded warranty deed, like the land
By decree of the water court
By the water right passing automatically with the land
By stock assignment and a new company certificate
questions.explanation: Mutual ditch company shares are personal property (stock), so they transfer by stock assignment and a new certificate from the company. Other water rights are conveyed with the same formalities as real estate, usually by recorded deed.

questions.stem: A buyer plans to water a large lawn and garden at a home served by a household-use-only exempt well. What should the broker tell the buyer?
choices: The permit allows lawn and garden watering up to one acre
Use is limited to indoors in one home; no outside watering
Exempt wells have no use limits once ownership changes
The buyer may water outside if the assessor approves
questions.explanation: A household-use-only permit generally covers indoor use in one home with no outside watering, and a buyer must stay within the permit's limits. Up to one acre of lawn and garden goes with a domestic and livestock well, usually on 35+ acres.

questions.stem: A Colorado homeowner believes the county set the home's actual value too high. Where does the owner file the first protest?
choices: With the county assessor
With the county board of equalization
With the Board of Assessment Appeals
With the county treasurer
questions.explanation: A value protest goes to the assessor first, then the county board of equalization, then the Board of Assessment Appeals, district court or arbitration.

questions.stem: A U.S. citizen who lives in Texas sells a Colorado rental house for $300,000 and signs no exemption affirmation. Which withholding applies at closing?
choices: Both FIRPTA and Colorado withholding
FIRPTA withholding only
Colorado nonresident withholding only
Neither, because the seller is a U.S. citizen
questions.explanation: Colorado withholding turns on Colorado residency, and a Texas resident is a nonresident. FIRPTA turns on foreign status, so it doesn't apply to a U.S. citizen.

questions.stem: A renter believes a landlord discriminated against him because of his sexual orientation. Within what time may he file a charge with the Colorado Civil Rights Division?
choices: Within 60 days
Within 180 days
Within two years
Within one year
questions.explanation: A charge with the CCRD may be filed within one year of the discriminatory act. Two years is the time for a private lawsuit, not the CCRD charge.

questions.stem: Which landlord is exempt from Colorado's source-of-income provisions?
choices: A landlord who owns three rental units
A landlord who checks credit only for voucher holders
A landlord whose units are all single-family homes
A landlord who owns ten rental units but self-manages
questions.explanation: Landlords with three or fewer rental units are exempt from the source-of-income provisions. A covered landlord may check credit only if it checks every prospective tenant, not just voucher holders.

questions.stem: After a public trustee foreclosure sale of her home, the former owner asks how long she has to redeem. What is accurate under current Colorado law?
choices: She has 75 days after the sale to redeem
She has no right to redeem after the sale
She may redeem until the confirmation deed is recorded
She has 8 business days to file a notice of intent to redeem
questions.explanation: The owner has no post-sale right of redemption in Colorado. Redemption belongs to junior lienors whose liens were recorded before the notice of election and demand, and they file notice within 8 business days.

questions.stem: In a typical Colorado foreclosure of a home loan, who serves as trustee under the deed of trust?
choices: A private trust company chosen by the lender
The county sheriff
The county public trustee
The lender's attorney
questions.explanation: In Colorado, the trustee under a deed of trust is a government official, the county public trustee, who conducts most foreclosures as non-judicial sales. Sheriff's sales occur only in the less common court foreclosures.

questions.stem: A foreclosure consultant agrees to negotiate a forbearance for a homeowner. Under the Colorado Foreclosure Protection Act, when may the consultant collect a fee?
choices: When the homeowner signs the written contract
After fully performing every promised service
After securing the fee with a lien on the home
Once the lender acknowledges receiving the request
questions.explanation: A foreclosure consultant may not collect any fee until every promised service has been fully performed, and may not take a lien or wage assignment to secure the fee.

questions.stem: A licensed broker lists for sale the home of an owner who is behind on the mortgage and facing foreclosure. Is the broker a foreclosure consultant under the CFPA?
choices: Yes, because the owner's loan is delinquent
Yes, unless the broker charges no commission
No, as long as the broker acts within the license
No, but only if the sale is a short sale
questions.explanation: A licensed real estate broker acting within the license, such as by listing the home for sale, is excluded from the definition of a foreclosure consultant.
